turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Honestly, a little stressed, but okay.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm a retired teacher and I just bought my first camera. I want to photograph birds in my garden.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Lovely hobby. A bird feeder near a window gives you a steady stream of subjects without scaring them off.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: They fly off as soon as

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Shoot from inside through an open window, or sit very still outside for ten minutes. Birds get used to a quiet person surprisingly fast.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And what setting should I use? They move so quickly.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Use a fast shutter speed, around one thousandth of a second, and burst mode. Then keep the sharpest shot.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Burst mode is the one that clicks a lot?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's the one. Hold the button down and it takes several photos per second.
